markdown_report:
The strongest provisional direction is **candidate-softmax training within the supplied corrected BERT4Rec**. No User Diagnosis or Model Diagnosis was supplied, so no proposal satisfies the required diagnosis-qualified selection rule. The recommendation below is an experimental hypothesis.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, terminal-prefix supervision matches appended-mask serving. Its target and all later interactions must remain absent from the bidirectional input. Second, protected dropout preserves recent observations while perturbing older context. Its benefit remains attributable only through matched deletion controls. Third, separately normalized terminal/interior losses make objective weights interpretable. Changing their reductions alongside the loss would confound the experiment.

**Insights from related work.** First, [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) motivates investigating sampled objectives. It does not establish that softmax improves this BERT4Rec benchmark. Second, [Correcting the LogQ Correction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) distinguishes deterministic positives from sampled negatives. This makes mixed in-batch sampling a less suitable first experiment because its correction requires additional accounting. Third, [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) motivates observable temporal context. Applying temporal features to BERT4Rec requires hiding supervised-target timestamps as carefully as target IDs.

**Framework and candidate assessment.** The three directions address complementary mechanisms: candidate competition, temporal relevance, and contextual robustness. Scores are Originality / Potential / User alignment / Model alignment / Difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Alignment is unavailable because diagnoses are absent.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Uniform candidate softmax | 3/6/NA/NA/3 | Small objective change; directly couples candidate rankings | Established method; sampled competition may reward popularity |
| Historical time-gap attention bias | 5/7/NA/NA/7 | Learns from observed spacing within one network | Additional architecture, timestamp handling, and serving-contract complexity |
| Protected-recent dropout | 3/5/NA/NA/2 | Minimal regularization with a clear control | Fixed recency protection may discard useful older context |

These assessments distinguish implementation promise from demonstrated utility; none has diagnosis-supported alignment.

**Provisional experiment.** At 40% progress, compare candidate softmax against the inherited loss using identical K=16 uniform negative draws, branch reductions, augmentation, and training schedule. Softmax makes each positive compete directly against its sampled alternatives. It is a candidate-ranking surrogate, without a claim of full-catalog likelihood calibration.

Implement `cross_entropy([positive_logit, negative_logits], target=0)` per supervised target, then retain example and branch averaging. Preserve duplicate negative draws and the supplied training-only exclusion policy. Keep raw model scores at inference, the reserved MASK, left padding, and final-nonpadding readout.

Train each arm independently from scratch, retaining one checkpoint per category and all four routes. Preserve seeds, 200 batches/epoch, the 200-epoch ceiling, predictor writer, and diagnostic interfaces. Select solely through host macro validation HR@10 within the shared budget. Report compute and all completed outcomes. Current diagnoses are required before asserting that this idea addresses two observed user failures and one measured model failure.

idea.description: Provisionally test K=16 uniform candidate-softmax training in corrected BERT4Rec, retaining one independently trained model and one selected checkpoint per category. This is not a diagnosis-qualified best idea because both supplied diagnoses are absent.
idea.motivation: Candidate softmax directly couples the positive score to sampled alternatives while leaving the BERT4Rec backbone and serving scores unchanged. The supplied historical gBCE score motivates objective research but cannot establish a causal advantage for this proposal. No observed user failure or measured model failure can honestly be attributed to the missing diagnoses.

Preserve the baseline exclusion set using training interactions only; exclude PAD, MASK and the target. Sample uniformly with replacement and retain duplicates. Do not introduce mixed in-batch sampling, LogQ corrections, temperature tuning, or additional scores in this first experiment. Candidate softmax is a sampled surrogate, not an unbiased full-catalog softmax estimator.

Withhold each terminal target and every later interaction; hide every supervised interior target. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, exactly 200 batches per epoch, at most 200 epochs, single-GPU execution, all four category routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Each arm starts from scratch and exports exactly one checkpoint per category; never combine arms or checkpoints.

Inference continues to score raw logits from intact histories plus an appended reserved MASK. Reserve room before truncation, left-pad, and read the greatest nonpadding index, never count-1. Preserve the canonical predictor writer and verify checkpoint, ModelView and exported predictor score parity. Keep view.model as the trained module and retain item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). The diagnostic loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative) with B x L tensors; internal multi-negative training must not alter that interface.

Record branch-specific sampled margins and negative-beats-positive rates on a fixed training diagnostic panel, with counts and definitions. These are proposed measurements, not supplied findings. Preserve the twenty-user simulator protocol without inventing preferences or traits. Only host macro validation HR@10 selects the experiment; include controls and failures in the 43,200 GPU-second budget. No unavailable metadata, extra datasets, pretrained weights, hidden test information or independently fitted component is used.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def candidate_softmax_loss(positive_logits, negative_logits):
    """Per-target sampled loss; duplicates remain separate candidates.

    positive_logits: (...,)
    negative_logits: (..., K)
    Caller supplies uniform training-only negatives and retains baseline
    valid-target, example, and terminal/interior reductions.
    """
    if negative_logits.ndim != positive_logits.ndim + 1:
        raise ValueError('Expected negative logits shaped (..., K)')
    if negative_logits.shape[:-1] != positive_logits.shape:
        raise ValueError('Positive and negative target dimensions differ')
    if negative_logits.shape[-1] < 1:
        raise ValueError('At least one negative is required')
    logits = torch.cat([
        positive_logits.float().unsqueeze(-1),
        negative_logits.float(),
    ], dim=-1)
    targets = torch.zeros(logits.shape[:-1], device=logits.device,
                          dtype=torch.long)
    return F.cross_entropy(
        logits.reshape(-1, logits.shape[-1]),
        targets.reshape(-1), reduction='none'
    ).reshape(positive_logits.shape)


# Integration specification: use the supplied corrected baseline source.
# Prespecify two independent arms: inherited loss and candidate softmax.
# Pair K=16 uniform-with-replacement negative draws across the arms.
# If this changes inherited sampling, disclose the common change.
# Use separate deterministic RNG streams so sampling and model dropout
# remain paired independently of loss computation.
#
# For each arm, independently, and for each of the four categories:
#   initialize ONE corrected BERT4Rec from scratch with training seed 42
#   for epoch in range(configured_epochs <= 200):
#       for step in range(200):
#           terminal, interior = supplied_leakage_free_sampler()
#           sample matched negatives with baseline training-only exclusions
#           compute inherited loss OR candidate_softmax_loss per target
#           Lt = baseline_example_reduction(terminal_target_losses)
#           Li = baseline_example_reduction(interior_target_losses)
#           optimize(inherited_alpha(epoch)*Lt + (1-inherited_alpha(epoch))*Li)
#       apply unchanged validation cadence and checkpoint policy
#   save ONE selected checkpoint with exact architecture configuration
#   export through the canonical predictor writer
#   verify trained/reloaded/ModelView/exported score parity
#   run compatible diagnostics with measured metrics and definitions
#
# Serving: observed history[-(maxlen-1):] + [MASK], then left padding.
# Read the final nonpadding position; score with raw model logits.
# DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; preprocessing seed remains 0.
# No score fusion, checkpoint averaging, or other-trial checkpoint reuse.

originality.positive: Provides a focused objective comparison in the corrected terminal/interior BERT4Rec setting.
originality.negative: Candidate softmax and sampled candidate competition are established techniques; benchmark-specific novelty is limited.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result could guide subsequent sampling research without increasing inference complexity.
future_potential.negative: Ranking improvements and diagnosis alignment are unverified, and sampled-negative gains may not transfer to full-catalog recommendations.

code_difficulty.positive: The loss requires a short stable implementation and no architectural or serving change.
code_difficulty.negative: Matched sampling, preserved reductions, diagnostic compatibility and faithful integration still require the absent baseline source.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Establishes masked-item training with a bidirectional Transformer for sequential recommendation.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed objective's advantage on the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Motivates investigating sampled BCE weighting and overconfidence in sequential recommendation.
limitations: Its evidence does not directly validate candidate softmax in corrected BERT4Rec.

related_work.title: Correcting the LogQ Correction
contributions: Examines sampling correction while distinguishing deterministically included positives from sampled negatives.
limitations: Mixed-sampler corrections require accounting beyond the proposed uniform candidate-softmax surrogate.

related_work.title: TiSASRec: Time Interval Aware Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Introduces historical time intervals into sequential attention.
limitations: Transfer to bidirectional masked BERT4Rec requires target-timestamp masking and compatible diagnostic interfaces.
